topics.title: complex exponential
topics.essence: e^(jωt) is a point going round the unit circle, ω radians every second. Cosine and sine are its two shadows.
topics.check: The phasor turns clockwise instead. Which of its two shadows can tell the difference?

topics.title: periodicity
topics.essence: A signal repeats when its phasor comes back to where it started. In continuous time it always does. In discrete time it does only if a whole number of steps makes a whole number of turns.
topics.check: Is e^(jn), one radian per step, periodic? What about e^(j2πn·3/8)?

topics.title: Fourier series
topics.essence: Any periodic signal is a sum of phasors spinning at whole multiples of one fundamental frequency.
topics.check: You make a square wave's period twice as long. What happens to the spacing of its harmonics on the frequency axis?

links.why: Let the angle grow with time, θ = ωt, and the point on the circle starts to turn.
The signal repeats each time the phasor completes a whole number of turns: ωT = 2π.
A Fourier coefficient is a projection: how much of the signal lies along one harmonic.
The harmonics are phasors e^(jkω₀t) that make k turns per period.
Only a signal that repeats can be built from whole-number multiples of one frequency.
